purpose.summary: Serve canonical confirmed transactions through the optional loopback Chronik HTTP surface with runtime admission, active-tip binding and explicit ownership.
scope: Register GET /tx/:txid only through the new host-query ABI; preserve the existing token-only ABI.
Serialize accepted-index mutations against nonblocking query leases without blocking validation callbacks or holding cs_main across disk I/O.
Reject stale, degraded, busy or pruned-storage reads; bind successful responses to the same accepted and active tip.
Release C++ payloads exactly once and retain one transaction permit through the HTTP body lifetime.
Extend public CI with ownership, shutdown, query-admission, rollback, restart, reindex, spent-coin and pruning falsification scenarios.
exclusions: No mempool, history, UTXO, spent-by lookup, websocket, plugin, wallet or full SDK compatibility claim.
No consensus, validation, activation, chain-selection, P2P, network identity or mainnet parameter change.
No duplicate transaction-body store, incoming evidence, private history, host-specific path, binary or cache.

commands: Configure the standalone node with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=OFF and inspect the generated bitcoind build graph.
expected_results: No observer, query admission or HTTP listener is reachable from the compiled-out node.

commands: Build test_bitcoin and bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON while leaving runtime observer opt-in disabled.
expected_results: The optional query bridge compiles, but creates no state, callbacks or listener without runtime opt-in.

commands: Run the locked offline Rust corpus, focused native query-admission/bridge/reader/envelope suites, and the four existing functional matrices from the reviewed public tree.
expected_results: Confirmed HTTP ownership, busy and failure behavior, canonical transaction bytes and lifecycle/pruning checks pass.

scenarios.command: Run the confirmed HTTP functional canary, live Rust host-service tests and native query-admission suite.
expected_results: Explicit loopback opt-in serves canonical confirmed ALP and non-coinbase spent-coin bytes. Invalid IDs are 400, missing confirmed IDs are 404, and busy/unavailable reads are 503.
Owned host allocations are released once, query/body permits are retained until completion, and shutdown joins host request work.
failure_conditions: Implicit listener or state, wrong protobuf, accepted stale/contradictory data, leaked or prematurely released host context, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Restart the HTTP canary node and compare the exact confirmed Tx bytes; run the retained-window observer restart scenario.
expected_results: Confirmed bytes remain identical after restart and no orphan or unbound response is served.
failure_conditions: Restart drift, stale query, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the HTTP and observer full-reindex canaries.
expected_results: Canonical confirmed bytes are unchanged after full reindex and query admission remains opt-in.
failure_conditions: Stale index, response drift, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the HTTP and observer chainstate-reindex canaries.
expected_results: Ordered accepted callbacks rebuild the same confirmed protobuf without changing validation.
failure_conditions: Stale index, response drift, validation effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the two-role pruning canary with fresh-pruned bootstrap and concurrent requests during already-indexed pruning.
expected_results: Concurrent old-transaction reads are either canonical 200 or protobuf 503, never a fabricated or partial response. After file removal the old transaction is 503; a retained recent transaction remains 200 and the node continues at its accepted height.
The pre-existing fresh-pruned observer bootstrap failure remains isolated from node correctness.
failure_conditions: Silent 404 for an indexed pruned transaction, fabricated fallback, partial result, node shutdown, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run observer deep-reorg failure, HTTP invalidate/reconsider and native query-close scenarios.
expected_results: Rolled-back transactions disappear from the confirmed route, reconsider restores exact bytes, and degraded or closing observation rejects new queries.
failure_conditions: Orphan result, stale observer state, query accepted after closure, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: Confirmed-only experimental local-regtest service; no mempool, history, UTXO or spend-state surface and no full Chronik SDK compatibility claim.
spent_by is absent, plugin maps are empty and finalization is false; an absent spent_by field does not mean an unspent output.
A successful response is a snapshot at its final active/indexed-tip check. A later reorganization can invalidate that snapshot.
Historical blk/rev availability is required. No duplicate body store or pruned-storage fallback is introduced.

Each transaction, spent-script aggregate and encoded result is limited to 64 MiB; parsing and cross-language copies can coexist in memory. One transaction-response permit prevents additional large results while its body bytes remain live.
Shutdown joins requests to protect the host context, but stalled storage I/O or a slow network client can delay graceful shutdown; no hard wall-clock shutdown bound is claimed.
Zero-value regtest spent coins do not establish an economically funded regtest profile.
Local compilation and component checks are not integrated Linux CI, independent reproduction, deployment or activation evidence.
counterevidence: Busy or lagging observation returns 503 even when the node already knows the transaction.
An indexed transaction whose canonical storage was pruned cannot be served and returns 503 instead of a fabricated result.
Incomplete spend/finality fields cannot support an unspentness or finality assertion.
A successful canonical snapshot cannot promise validity after a subsequent reorganization.
